status: drafted by coder, awaiting Jithin's review
note: Each case lists the space ids a knowledgeable person would accept as the TOP route for that student. An empty list means the right answer is no route at all. The accepted sets are the coder's judgment from the space documents; Jithin should correct them from what he knows of the spaces. Remember that code sorts routes that are open to the student ahead of ask-first ones, so the top route depends on the audience.

cases.idea: A small wooden stand that holds my phone at an angle on my desk. Fits in my hand. I need one.
cases.why: Laser-cut plywood or a 3D print; both at the Maker Space.

cases.idea: An engraved acrylic sign with our club's name, about 12 inches wide, for a tabling booth. One sign.
cases.why: Laser cutting. BME is not open to a non-Viterbi student, so the Maker Space must be first.

cases.idea: A palm-sized night light for my dorm desk with a warm LED inside and a 3D printed cover. Just one.
cases.why: Electronics plus 3D printing; both spaces have both.

cases.idea: A small box to hold a Raspberry Pi and a temperature sensor I will solder to it. Shoebox size or smaller, one of them.
cases.why: 3D printed or laser-cut box plus soldering.

cases.idea: A cardboard scale model of a building for my architecture studio, cut from flat sheets. About backpack size.
cases.why: Laser-cut cardboard; only the Maker Space lists cardboard, and BME is not open to this student.

cases.idea: A very detailed miniature figurine about 2 inches tall for a board game. I need fine detail on the face.
cases.why: Fine detail points to the resin printer, which only the Maker Space lists.

cases.idea: A simple wooden shelf for three small plants that hangs on my wall. About two feet long. It has to hold their weight.
cases.why: Wood cut with power tools or the laser cutter at the Maker Space.

cases.idea: A small aluminum bracket to mount a light on my bike. It has to hold weight and survive rain.
cases.why: Metalworking: both spaces list a machine shop. A strong 3D print at the Maker Space is also acceptable.

cases.idea: I have a guitar effects pedal kit and need to solder the parts onto the circuit board and test it.
cases.why: Soldering. BME is not open to this student, so the Maker Space must be first.

cases.idea: I want to record a podcast episode with two friends about campus food. We need microphones and a quiet room.
cases.why: Non-engineering idea. The Digital Creative Lab's page lists podcast studios open to students.

cases.idea: For my anthropology seminar I am recording spoken interviews with three alumni and need a quiet place to record clean audio.
cases.why: Non-engineering idea. Audio recording: the podcast studios.

cases.idea: My theatre class is making a ten-minute radio play. We need somewhere to record four voices.
cases.why: Non-engineering idea. Audio recording: the podcast studios.

cases.idea: I am an English major with an idea for a digital storytelling project. I have never used any of this technology and would like a workshop or someone to show me what is possible.
cases.why: Non-engineering idea. The Ahmanson Lab's page offers technology, services and workshops to USC students; no other listed space offers workshops for a beginner outside engineering. Its equipment is not listed, so the right route says to ask its staff.

cases.idea: Our club is starting a podcast. We need to record the first episode and also make a small acrylic sign with the show's logo for our table.
cases.why: Two needs. Either the studio or the laser cutter is acceptable as the top route, as long as both needs are covered.

cases.idea: I want to sew a canvas tote bag with a zipper pocket.
cases.why: No listed space has sewing equipment. The right answer is no route, with a reason.
